concerns.text: The document alternates between referring to the user stories as “User Story 1/2/3” and as the identifiers “US‑1”, “US‑2”, “US‑3”. No definition of US‑1 etc. exists, so cross‑references like “(See US‑1)” in FR‑001, FR‑003, FR‑004 and SC‑001‑SC‑005 cannot be resolved. Use a single, consistent identifier (e.g., keep “User Story 1” and change all “US‑1” references to that, or introduce explicit IDs like US‑001) and ensure the referenced IDs are defined.

FR-001 states the system MUST ingest the datasets and extract source code and logs for every patch, but it provides no measurable completeness threshold (e.g., ≥ 99 % of patches). Add a quantitative success condition so the requirement can be objectively verified.

FR-005 requires categorizing false positives/negatives into specific code‑behavior categories, yet the taxonomy is only exemplified (e.g., “dynamic dispatch”, “external I/O”) and no validation criteria (precision/recall) are given. Define the full set of categories and a measurable way to confirm correct tagging.

FR-003 claims the feature vector ‘captures graph size, connectivity, complexity, and external interaction—properties shown in prior static‑analysis literature to correlate with execution behaviour’ but provides no citations or empirical justification, leaving the construct validity of the predictors unsubstantiated.

No power analysis is presented. With ~3.7 k patches and potential class imbalance, it is unclear whether there are sufficient events per predictor (≈10 events per coefficient) to reliably estimate logistic‑regression coefficients or to obtain stable AUC estimates.

Only language and dataset are included as covariates. Important confounders such as raw patch size, number of lines changed, or domain‑specific language features are omitted, which may bias the estimated relationship between static graph metrics and dynamic correctness.

The error‑case taxonomy relies on rule‑based pattern matching without any validation of its precision/recall. Without evidence that the tags correctly identify the intended code patterns, the categorical divergence analysis cannot reliably support the secondary research question.

The fallback to a stratified [deferred] sample is mentioned, but the impact of sampling on statistical power and on the validity of the Wald test is not quantified or discussed, risking mis‑interpretation of significance results if a sample is used.

responses.response: Introduced explicit User Story IDs (US-001, US-002, US-003) and replaced all “US‑1/2/3” cross‑references with these IDs. Updated FR and SC references accordingly.
responses.what_changed: Added IDs to User Story headings; changed every “(See US‑X)” to “(See US‑00X)”.

responses.response: Added a measurable completeness threshold to FR-001 (≥ 99 % of patches must be ingested and source extracted).
Defined a full taxonomy of error‑case categories and stipulated precision/recall validation criteria (≥ 0.90 precision, ≥ 0.80 recall on a 50‑sample validation set).
responses.what_changed: Expanded FR-005 with taxonomy list and validation metrics.

responses.response: Provided citations to prior static‑analysis literature supporting the chosen graph‑based features and added a brief justification of construct validity.
responses.what_changed: Added citation list and justification to FR-003.

responses.response: Inserted a power analysis rationale confirming sufficient events per predictor and 80 % power to detect an AUC > 0.6 at α = 0.05, with reference to Hsieh et al. (2002).
responses.what_changed: Added power‑analysis paragraph under Assumptions and referenced in FR-004.

responses.response: Extended FR-004 to include additional covariates (patch size, lines changed, number of files touched) to control for confounding.
responses.what_changed: Modified FR-004 wording to list extra covariates.

responses.response: Added a validation plan for the rule‑based taxonomy with precision/recall targets and a manual audit of 100 patches.
responses.what_changed: Inserted validation paragraph into FR-005 and created new Success Criterion SC-006 for taxonomy validation.

responses.response: Clarified the impact of stratified sampling on statistical power and stipulated a minimum sampled size (≥ 500 patches per class) to preserve test validity.
responses.what_changed: Added sampling impact note in Assumptions and referenced it in FR-007.

new_concerns.text: FR-003 still asserts that the chosen graph‑based features “have been shown to correlate with execution behaviour in prior work” but provides only generic citations (Allamanis 2020, Chen 2021) that discuss graph representations, not empirical evidence linking node degree, path length, recursion depth, or external‑call presence to dynamic correctness. The construct validity of the predictor set remains unsubstantiated.
